recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-13515 unless a future work group decision changes DataRequirement limit/sort semantics or reintroduces a distinct total-result-limit parameter.
issue_request: FHIR-13515 was a Published FHIR-core/STU3 change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking to add DataRequirement.limit and DataRequirement.sort so requirements such as "most recent 5 results" can be represented, and initially proposing a _limit search parameter.
initial_application: The source history shows commit bdd81c800a6fd72a8ce35e0bde6e33c75e51314b, matching Jira comment SVN 13443, added DataRequirement.limit, DataRequirement.sort, DataRequirement.sort.path, DataRequirement.sort.direction, and the SortDirection code list. A later Jira comment records SVN 14042 and says there was no need to define _limit because _count does the same.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively maps datarequirement to metadatatypes, placing source/datatypes/datarequirement.xml in current build scope. Current source/search.html defines _count and states that _sort plus _count can return the latest matching resource. FHIR-15746, FHIR-15747, and FHIR-15748 were applied in the same historical commit but concern separate subject/canonical datatype changes and were not decided here.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The authoritative DataRequirement source already has the limit/sort structure requested by the issue, and the proposed _limit search parameter is intentionally not present because _count covers the requested behavior.
